title: How to upload documents for an online application
summary: This page explains how to prepare and upload documents when applying for a NSW Government service online.
intro:
When you apply for a NSW Government service or support, you might need to provide details from a document to confirm your identity or prove your eligibility. Sometimes we'll ask you to upload a copy of the document to confirm your details.

Make sure your name, address and all the details requested are clearly visible when you submit your documents.
what_you_need: The document must clearly show your name, address, and all requested details.
Digital documents should be saved and uploaded as files.
Paper documents should be scanned or photographed, and the resulting file should be saved and uploaded.
Photos of documents should be saved as JPEG, JPG, PDF, PNG, or TIF files.

faqs.q: What details must be visible when I submit my documents?
faqs.a: Ensure that your name, address, and all requested details are clearly visible on the documents you submit.

faqs.q: What are the requirements for the file name and format?
faqs.a: The file must be saved in the requested format (such as JPEG, JPG, PDF, PNG, or TIF), be less than 6 MB, and include only letters and numbers in the file name (no spaces or special characters).

faqs.q: How should I handle digital documents?
faqs.a: If you have digital documents, ask the provider to email you a copy, save the attachments to your device, and then upload them when you apply online.

faqs.q: How do I upload documents if I only have photos?
faqs.a: If you take a photo of documents, email the photo to yourself, open the email on a computer or tablet, and save the image as a JPEG, JPG, PDF, PNG, or TIF file before uploading.
